lead: four trades, and you were doing the work in each of them before there was a job to apply for. three ended without a taper, and everyone who first let you in still gets an hour of your week.
sun: a trade ends here the way a season ends. no notice worked out with a hand kept in, no advisory afternoon a year later, no good client's number held in case — the whole apparatus goes inside a fortnight and never comes up again. it costs almost nothing, because the part of the work you were built for was finished by the ninth month anyway.
moon: you are only ever good at the first month — arriving before the request, doing the thing while everyone else is still working out who to ask. the second year of a job has never belonged to you. so the shedding is cheap. the door is not. arriving early only works where somebody has already decided to let you through it.
pull: you have never been in the fourth year of anything. the four who let you in early are the only people your working life kept, and you no longer work with any of them.
tension: the interview turns on why you left, and the answer that is true — it was finished — cannot be said in a room hiring for the long haul. so you hand over a shape people recognise: money, a manager, a move. every trade you have entered was entered on a soft account of the last one, by somebody who has never been a day late on anything owed.
cost: four working lives have left nothing to get over, so the next first morning arrives at full appetite — a thing most people are handed once and you have had four times. what does not happen is accumulation. a decade of it produced no rank anywhere and four people permanently owed for a door they opened to somebody who no longer exists.

lead: you left at nineteen, whole — the town, the name they had for you, the person who sat at that table. one of them still gets every practical thing you have, and none has heard the reason.
sun: no gradient is available, so a family cannot be left in the order it deserves. the one who did it and the two who did nothing went in the same season, at the same speed, on the same silence. no birthdays, no half-attendance, nothing kept warm for later. what did not break is one obligation, and it runs at full service — the money moves, the appointments get made, the forms come out right.
moon: nobody else can set the date on it, and you have not set one. what happened in that house is intact in you — the sequence in order, the words as they were said — and not a year of it has faded. so the family works from the only version anybody ever put in front of them, in which you got above your people and stopped coming.
pull: the one who earned the leaving and the ones who did not were shed at the same rate, in the same month, and only you know there was a difference.
tension: your sister has an explanation thirty years old and it is wrong in every part except the date. correcting it means producing the thing, now, to people who were children at the time and to one person old enough that it would be the last real conversation available with them. so the wrong account stands, and you keep doing the paperwork, and every practical kindness you perform confirms for everyone that nothing much can have happened.
cost: nobody in that family sat through a withdrawal. the going took one season and left them nothing to manage afterwards, and the one owed gets paid in full without ever having to ask twice. the two who did nothing got the identical treatment, and the only relation of yours that survived is made entirely of duty: you can be reported to, and you cannot be visited.

lead: the whole of it went in one season — the business, the way you lived, and whoever you were while it worked — and what survived was never the one figure everyone outside still says out loud.
sun: when it went it went whole. the smaller version of the same thing under a new name was available and you did not take it, and the good half was saleable and you did not keep it, and none of it is coming up again. what came through untouched is what was owed — the arithmetic nobody believes, in which the assets were the perishable item and the debts were the permanent one.
moon: from any distance it is one event with one number attached. up close it is six arrangements made in six years — a relative who has never once mentioned it, a friend who lent against nothing, a silent half-partner who never used the word — and only the collapse sorted which of them were real. you are the only person holding the list.
pull: everyone outside is discussing a figure. what is actually outstanding is six names on six different sets of terms, and the largest of them was a handshake in a car park.
tension: the offer comes from somebody who loves you — name the figure and it goes away. no figure does. paying the biggest first is what any accountant would do, and it leaves the friend who lent against nothing standing longest, which is unbearable and correct. so you rank your creditors by how far they trusted you, tell nobody that is the method, and take being called disorganised by people who could settle it in an afternoon.
cost: the loss was taken in one piece — no shell of the old thing kept running to look solvent, no quiet salvage, nothing dragged into the new life. six obligations came through the season at full size, and none has been discounted to fit what you now earn. those six are the only people with evidence that the old life happened, and each holds a sixth of it.

lead: nineteen years since the last one and not a partial one in all of them — no sip, no exception, no bad week. the wanting is the size it was that morning, one length behind you, keeping pace.
sun: stopping was never the hard version. moderation was the impossible one — a unit count, the one drink you are allowed at a wedding, all of it unavailable, because nothing here comes off in percentages. so the one who drank ended inside a week and has not been seen since. what did not end is the promise, made out loud, in a kitchen, to one person who was standing there.
moon: the appetite does not shed with the life it belonged to. it has held the same width for nineteen years — never closing, never falling away, in no worse condition now than on the last night — and it keeps the detail perfectly: the hour, the weight of the glass, the particular relief of the second one. nothing in you has ever let a wanted thing go dim.
pull: she left in the eighth year. the promise did not, and the thirst did not, and the two of them have been keeping each other company ever since.
tension: people who arrived after read a temperament — someone who simply does not, the way others do not smoke. the ones who were there hand you the anniversary. saying the true thing at this range, that you want one exactly as much as on the last night, turns the room into a vigil for a relapse that is not coming. so the wanting has had no witness in nineteen years, and it is the steadiest thing in you.
cost: it was settled in a week and has asked nothing of you since — no unit ever counted, no evening negotiated — which is a freedom the people who taper never get. the one it was promised to has been gone eleven years and could not release you from it if she walked in tomorrow. so the keeping goes on, at full thirst, for a household that no longer exists.
